title: Ladder A priority probe: finite-difference step-size sweep on A1 NACA0012 dCD/dshape
purpose: Four Ladder-A rung verdicts (A1, A2, A4, A5) have been graded against a 1-12% shape-derivative FD tolerance band that was inferred from A1 alone (11.43%) and never step-swept. A2 later achieved 1.71% on a larger mesh with more DVs, showing the band is too loose. This probe sweeps the central-difference step size on A1 itself to determine whether A1's 11.43% is a step-size artifact (adjoint fine) or a real, step-independent gradient defect (adjoint has a real error), and to derive a defensible FD tolerance from data instead of a single n=1 point.

case.name: ladder-a1-naca0012
case.objective_checked: scenario1.aero_post.CD wrt dvs.shape (8 FFD shape DVs)
case.script: fdStepSweep.py (new, this probe) -- same daOptions/meshOptions/Top class as runScript.py; only the central-difference step size varies across invocations. For each step: 1 baseline run_model, 1 compute_totals (adjoint, all 8 components), then 8 x (plus/minus run_model) central differences, one component perturbed at a time with all others held at 0 -- identical in substance to what OpenMDAO's check_totals does internally.
case.rel_err_formula: norm(Jan - Jfd) / norm(Jfd), the same metric OpenMDAO's check_totals prints as 'Relative Error (Jan - Jfd) / Jfd' -- verified byte-for-byte against check_totals_run2.log at step=1e-3 (11.427% reproduced independently to 5 significant figures, minor tail digits differ due to normal run-to-run floating point, same as this stack's documented ~16-sig-fig reproducibility).

adjoint_8vector_CD_wrt_shape.note: Recomputed fresh at every one of the 12 step invocations; bit-stable to 7+ significant figures across all runs -- adjoint determinism is not in question.

ok -- coincidental low point, see interpretation

failures_recorded_honestly.result: container exited 1 mid-run (crashed during idx0/idx1 perturbed solves, ~19s in, no OOM/error signature found in dmesg or docker events -- likely a transient container/mesh-redecompose race)
failures_recorded_honestly.action: retried once with identical command, retry succeeded cleanly and produced the value used in the table (fdsweep_1e-5_retry.log). The failed attempt's log (fdsweep_1e-5.log) is kept on disk, not deleted, not used for any number.

failures_recorded_honestly.result: genuine, reproducible-in-character solver failure: primal residual stalled at 4.8e-5 for idx6 (+0.05 perturbation), never reaching the 1e-8 tolerance within the 1000-iteration cap. This is a real numerical failure of the SIMPLE solver at that shape magnitude for that specific control point (the leading-edge combo mode), not a script bug -- idx0-idx5 converged fine at the same step.

per_component_relative_error_pct_vs_step.note: (fd - adjoint) / adjoint, per component, per step. idx0, idx1, idx6 are the three components PROOF.md previously localized as disagreeing (idx0, idx1 near the leading edge; idx6 the leading-edge combo mode). idx2,3,4,5,7 are the other five.

squared_error_contribution_pct_at_step_1.note: idx6 alone accounts for 82.7% of the squared (Jan-Jfd) norm at A1's original step -- matches PROOF.md's independently-derived 82.7% exactly.

curve_shape_verdict.full_8component_vector_norm: NOT a clean V and NOT flat -- noisy/non-monotonic across the well-converged plateau (1e-3 to 3e-2): 11.43% -> 11.52% -> 10.47% -> 8.94% -> 4.28% (2e-2) -> 9.83% (3e-2), then primal breakdown at 5e-2. Below 1e-4 it rises monotonically and steeply (11.5% -> 17.6% -> 52.9% -> 95.0%) as roundoff takes over, which IS classic FD V-curve behavior on the small-step side. The dip to 4.28% at step=2e-2 is a coincidental crossing, not a genuine converged minimum: it is caused entirely by idx6's erratic, sign-unstable FD estimate passing near the adjoint's magnitude at that one step before overshooting 2x by 3e-2 and causing outright primal-solver failure by 5e-2. There is no step at which idx6 is a stable, trustworthy FD estimate.
curve_shape_verdict.excluding_idx0_idx1_idx6: FLAT and low across the entire well-converged plateau: 2.99% (1e-4), 2.69% (1e-3), 2.64% (5e-3), 2.61% (1e-2), 2.54% (2e-2), 2.48% (3e-2). Cosine similarity 0.99998 at every one of those steps. This is the textbook 'flat curve = real agreement, not noise' signature -- for 5 of 8 components the harness and adjoint are demonstrably sound and step-independent.
curve_shape_verdict.idx0_and_idx1_individually: Flat and step-independent across 1e-6 to 3e-2: idx0 sits at -8% to -14%, idx1 at -1% to -16% (excluding the 5e-2 outlier which is itself inside a failing solve). This is a real, stable, step-independent disagreement, not roundoff noise -- it does not shrink as step shrinks through the well-converged window.
curve_shape_verdict.idx6_individually: Sign-flipped (wrong sign vs adjoint) and magnitude-unstable across nearly the entire usable range: -88% to -119% relative error from step=1e-6 through 1e-2, briefly crossing correct order-of-magnitude near 2e-2, then overshooting to +110% at 3e-2, then the solver itself fails to converge at 5e-2 for this exact component. No step size produces a trustworthy idx6 estimate.

verdict.is_11.43pct_a_stepsize_artefact: NO, predominantly. idx6 alone drives 74-83% of the squared-difference norm at every well-converged step tested, and its FD estimate is unstable/wrong-signed everywhere except a narrow coincidental crossing near step=2e-2 -- not a resolvable, step-independent gradient. idx0 and idx1 contribute a further ~10-16% of the norm and disagree by a STABLE ~9-16% across 3+ decades of step size (1e-6 to 3e-2), which is definitionally not a step-size artifact (a step artifact would shrink toward zero somewhere in that window; this doesn't). The correct reading is the FLAT-CURVE branch of the task's own decision rule: 'the disagreement is real and step-independent, i.e. something in the gradient' -- for 3 of 8 components, exactly matching and independently reconfirming PROOF.md's prior leading-edge localization (idx0, idx1 near the LE, idx6 the LE combo mode itself).
verdict.is_any_of_it_a_stepsize_artefact: Partially, at the margins only. A1's original step (1e-3) is inside the well-converged plateau, not in the roundoff-dominated regime, so its 11.43% was not itself corrupted by a bad step choice -- but the plateau's aggregate number is genuinely noisy step-to-step (8.9% to 11.5%) purely as a byproduct of idx6's instability, meaning the raw vector-norm percentage is a fragile statistic that swings for reasons unrelated to step quality. The 5 well-behaved components (excl. idx0/1/6) are unaffected by step choice within 1e-4 to 3e-2 and agree to ~2.5-3.0% throughout -- confirming the harness itself (same conclusion the geometric-constraint and flow-parameter derivatives already supported).
verdict.cross_validation_against_PROOF_md: Exact agreement with the prior, independently-run investigation: squared-error contribution of idx6 at step=1e-3 here is 82.70% vs PROOF.md's 82.7%; cosine excluding idx0/1/6 here is 0.999983 vs PROOF.md's 0.999983; cosine including all 8 here is 0.993451 vs PROOF.md's 0.993452. This probe was run fresh, independently, from a different script, and reproduces PROOF.md's numbers to 5-6 significant figures -- strong confirmation neither run was a fluke.

recommended_fd_step_size.basis: Below ~1e-4 the CD difference between +/-step perturbations falls below the primal's residual noise floor (primalMinResTol=1e-8) and the FD derivative degrades monotonically and severely (11.5% -> 95% relative error from 1e-4 down to 1e-8). Above ~3e-2 the shape perturbation is large enough that the leading-edge control points (idx6 specifically) push the mesh/primal solver into non-convergence (documented failures at 5e-2 and 1e-1). 1e-3 to 1e-2 is the widest window in which every one of the 8 components produces a real, converged central-difference estimate; A1's original choice of 1e-3 was already inside this safe window, so the step choice itself was not the problem.

recommended_fd_tolerance_for_grading_fut.value: Do not grade on the aggregate vector-norm relative-error percentage alone. Report (a) vector-norm relative error at a step confirmed to be in the well-converged plateau (verified by a 2-3 point step check, not assumed), AND (b) per-component or cosine-similarity agreement, AND (c) a flag on any component whose FD estimate changes sign or moves by >50% of its own magnitude across one decade of step size (that is the idx6 signature and it is diagnostic of a real defect, not noise). For a case with NO such flagged components, this dataset shows the achievable, harness-sound floor is approximately 2.5-5% vector-norm relative error (2.5-3.0% here at 4032 cells; A2 independently achieved 1.71% at 38304 cells with 96 DVs, consistent with the floor tightening on finer meshes/more DVs). Recommend a PASS band of <=5% vector-norm error WITH no flagged components, a CONDITIONAL band of 5-15% requiring a per-component breakdown before grading, and treat >15% or any sign-flipped/unstable component as FAIL pending investigation regardless of the aggregate percentage. The previously used 1-12% band is retired: its sole supporting data point (A1's 11.43%) is now shown to be a number in which one badly-conditioned component contributes 74-83% of the squared error, which is not what '1-12% is normal, generically fine variation' implies.
recommended_fd_tolerance_for_grading_fut.old_band_retired: 1-12%, inferred from A1 alone (n=1), now shown to conflate a genuine ~2.5-3% harness-sound floor with an 83%-idx6-driven sign-flip defect and a stable ~10-16% two-component bias -- three different phenomena averaged into one misleading aggregate number.

a4_verdict_reassessment.a4_reported: 10.04% CD wrt shape FD error, 1 scalar shape DV, 2777 cells, previously graded PASS under the retired 1-12% band
a4_verdict_reassessment.was_a4_itself_step_swept: No -- this probe only swept A1. No A4-specific step-size data exists.
a4_verdict_reassessment.reasoning: A4 has a single scalar shape DV, so it cannot exhibit A1's vector-norm dilution/cancellation dynamics (there is no 'idx6 dominates the squared-error norm' effect possible with one component) -- A4's 10.04% is a raw, undiluted single-component disagreement. In THIS case, the two components with a genuine, stable, step-independent disagreement (idx0, idx1) sit at 9-16% relative error across 3+ decades of step -- i.e. a single shape component in this problem class CAN legitimately carry a real, non-artifactual ~10% disagreement that no step-size choice resolves. A4's 10.04% falls squarely in that same numeric range, not in the harness-sound ~2.5-5% floor this probe established for well-behaved components. Nothing here proves A4's adjoint is wrong -- A4 is a different case (Ahmed body, different mesh, different FFD) and no equivalent step sweep or per-component check has been run on it.
a4_verdict_reassessment.verdict: A4's PASS should be DOWNGRADED to CONDITIONAL / UNVERIFIED, not left standing and not flipped to FAIL. The sole basis for its original PASS (the 1-12% band inferred from A1 alone) is retired by this probe's findings. A4's own number (10.04%) sits at a level this probe now associates with real, step-independent per-component defects rather than clean agreement, in the one case (A1) where the composition has actually been examined. Recommended next action: run this same step-size-sweep protocol (1e-3, 1e-2, plus a roundoff check at 1e-5 and a large-step check at ~3e-2) directly on A4 before re-confirming or reversing its verdict.

hard_rules_compliance.no_fabricated_numbers: Every value in sweep_table and per_component tables is read directly from a completed docker/mpirun DAFoam run's stdout, logged to demo-output/website/dafoam/ladder-a/logs_A1_stepsize/ (see file list). Failed steps (5e-2, 1e-1) are reported as failures with the partial data actually obtained, not filled in or estimated.
hard_rules_compliance.single_variable_only: Only the central-difference step size (-step argument) was varied across the 12 runs. daOptions, meshOptions, mesh, MPI rank count (2), primalMinResTol (1e-8), and the Top class/FFD/DV setup are byte-identical to A1's own runScript.py in every invocation.
hard_rules_compliance.processorN_trap: Encountered and handled per the known trap: 'sudo rm -rf processor0 processor1 processor*' was run before every single docker invocation in this probe.
hard_rules_compliance.nothing_left_running: All docker containers exited (--rm); verified with 'docker ps -a' showing zero running containers at the end of this probe. processor0/processor1 directories removed after the final run.
